text: Let $\mathrm{p},\mathrm{q}\in \mathrm{ℝ}$ and $\left (1-\sqrt{3}i\right )^{200}=2^{199}(p+iq),i=\sqrt{-1}$ then $\mathrm{p}+\mathrm{q}+\mathrm{q}^{2}$ and $\mathrm{p}-\mathrm{q}+\mathrm{q}^{2}$ are roots of the equation.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left (1-\sqrt{3}i\right )^{200}$

$=\left [2\left (\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right )\right ]^{200}$

$=2^{200}\left (\cos \frac{π}{3}-i\sin \frac{π}{3}\right )^{200}$

$=2^{200}\left (\cos \frac{200π}{3}-i\sin \frac{200π}{3}\right )$

$=2^{200}\left (\cos \left (66π+\frac{2π}{3}\right )-i\sin \left (66π+\frac{2π}{3}\right )\right )$

$=2^{200}\left (\cos \frac{2π}{3}-i\sin \frac{2π}{3}\right )$

$=2^{200}\left (-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right )$

$=2^{199}\left (-1-\sqrt{3}i\right )$

$=2^{199}(p+iq)$

$\therefore$ p = $-$1 and q = $-\sqrt{3}$

Now, $p-q+q^{2}=-1+\sqrt{3}+3=2+\sqrt{3}=α$

and $p+q+q^{2}=-1-\sqrt{3}+3=2-\sqrt{3}=β$

$\therefore$ $α+β=4$

$αβ=\left (2+\sqrt{3}\right )\left (2-\sqrt{3}\right )=4-3=1$

$\therefore$ Quadratic equation is

$x^{2}-(α+β)x+αβ=0$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}-4x+1=0$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
Let N denote the number that turns up when a fair die is rolled. If the probability that the system of equations

$x+y+z=1$

$2x+\mathrm{N}y+2z=2$

$3x+3y+\mathrm{N}z=3$

has unique solution is $\frac{k}{6}$, then the sum of value of k and all possible values of N is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For unique solution $\Delta \neq 0$

i.e. $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & N & 2 \\ 3 & 3 & N \end{array}\right |\neq 0$

$\Rightarrow \left (N^{2}-6\right )-(2N-6)+(6-3N)\neq 0$

$\Rightarrow N^{2}-5N+6\neq 0$

$\therefore N\neq 2$ and $N\neq 3$

$\therefore$ Probability of not getting 2 or 3 in a throw of dice $=\frac{2}{3}$

As given $\frac{2}{3}=\frac{k}{6}\Rightarrow k=4$

$\therefore$ Required value $=1+4+5+6+4=20$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: The relation $\mathrm{R}=\{(\mathrm{a},\mathrm{b}):\gcd (\mathrm{a},\mathrm{b})=1,2\mathrm{a}\neq \mathrm{b},\mathrm{a},\mathrm{b}\in \mathrm{ℤ}\}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

(a, b) belongs to relation R if $\gcd (a,b)=1,2a\neq b$.

Here $\gcd$ means greatest common divisor. $\gcd$ of two numbers is the largest number that divides both of them.

(1) For Reflexive,

In $aRa,\qquad \gcd (a,a)=a$

$\therefore$ This relation is not reflexive.

(2) For Symmetric:

Take $a=2,b=1\Rightarrow \gcd (2,1)=1$
Also $2a=4\neq b$

Now $\gcd (b,a)=1$ $\Rightarrow \gcd (1,2)=1$

and 2b should not be equal to a

But here, $2b=2=a$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ is not Symmetric

(3) For Transitive:

Let $\mathrm{a}=14,\mathrm{b}=19,\mathrm{c}=21$

$\gcd (\mathrm{a},\mathrm{b})=1,2a\neq b$

$\gcd (\mathrm{b},\mathrm{c})=1,2b\neq c$

$\gcd (\mathrm{a},\mathrm{c})=7,2a\neq c$

Hence not transitive

$\Rightarrow R$ is neither symmetric nor transitive.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: $\lim _{t\to 0}\left (1^{\frac{1}{\sin 2t}}+2^{\frac{1}{\sin 2t}}+...+n^{\frac{1}{\sin 2t}}\right )^{\sin ^{2}t}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $k=\dfrac{1}{\sin ^{2}t}$; as $t\to 0$, $k\to \infty$, and the expression is $\left (1^{k}+2^{k}+\cdots +n^{k}\right )^{1/k}$.

Taking $n^{k}$ out of the bracket,

$\left (1^{k}+2^{k}+\cdots +n^{k}\right )^{1/k}=nS^{1/k},S=\left (\frac{1}{n}\right )^{k}+\left (\frac{2}{n}\right )^{k}+\cdots +\left (\frac{n-1}{n}\right )^{k}+1.$

Each of the $n$ terms of $S$ lies in $(0,1]$ and the last one is 1, so $1\leq S\leq n$ and $1\leq S^{1/k}\leq n^{1/k}$.

As $k\to \infty$, $n^{1/k}\to 1$, so $S^{1/k}\to 1$ and the limit equals $n$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: $\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1+\sqrt{3}}{3+\sqrt{3}}\right )+\sec ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{\frac{8+4\sqrt{3}}{6+3\sqrt{3}}}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1+\sqrt{3}}{3+\sqrt{3}}\right )+\sec ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{\frac{8+4\sqrt{3}}{6+3\sqrt{3}}}\right )$

$=\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1+\sqrt{3}}{3+\sqrt{3}}\right )+\sec ^{-1}\left (\frac{16+8\sqrt{3}}{12+6\sqrt{3}}\right )^{\frac{1}{2}}$

$=\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1+\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)}\right )+\sec ^{-1}\left (\frac{4(1^{2}+(\sqrt{3})^{2}+2.1.\sqrt{3})}{3^{2}+(\sqrt{3})^{2}+2.3.\sqrt{3}}\right )^{\frac{1}{2}}$

$=\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )+\sec ^{-1}\left (\frac{4(\sqrt{3}+1)^{2}}{(3+\sqrt{3})^{2}}\right )^{\frac{1}{2}}$

$=\frac{π}{6}+\sec ^{-1}\left (\frac{2(\sqrt{3}+1)}{\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)}\right )$

$=\frac{π}{6}+\sec ^{-1}\left (\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right )$

$=\frac{π}{6}+\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )$

$=\frac{π}{6}+\frac{π}{6}$

$=\frac{π}{3}$

text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $x^{3}dy+(xy-1)dx=0,x>0,y\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=3-\mathrm{e}$. Then y (1) is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{3}dy+xydx-dx=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1-xy}{x^{3}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{y}{x^{2}}=\frac{1}{x^{3}}$

I.F. $=e^{\int \frac{dx}{x2}}=e^{-\frac{1}{x}}$

$\therefore ye^{-\frac{1}{x}}=\int \frac{e^{-\dfrac{1}{x}}}{x^{3}}dx$

For RHS put $-\frac{1}{x}=t\Rightarrow \frac{dx}{x^{2}}=dt$

$\therefore ye^{-\frac{1}{x}}=-\int te^{t}dt$

$\Rightarrow ye^{-\frac{1}{x}}=-\left [te^{t}-e^{t}\right ]+c$

$\Rightarrow ye^{-\frac{1}{x}}=\frac{e^{-\dfrac{1}{x}}}{x}+e^{-\frac{1}{x}}+c$

$↓y\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=3-e$

$\Rightarrow (3-e)e^{-2}=2e^{-2}+e^{-2}+c$

$\Rightarrow \quad c=-\frac{1}{e}$

For $y(1)$ put $x=1,c=-e^{-1}$ in equation (i) we get $ye^{-1}=e^{-1}+e^{-1}-e^{-1}$

$\Rightarrow y=1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
Let $\Omega$ be the sample space and $\mathrm{A}\subseteq \Omega$ be an event.

Given below are two statements :

(S1) : If P(A) = 0, then A = $𝜙$

(S2) : If P(A) = 1, then A = $\Omega$

Then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By the classical definition of probability (a finite sample space of equally likely outcomes), $P(A)=\frac{n(A)}{n(\Omega )}$.

(S1): $P(A)=0\Rightarrow n(A)=0\Rightarrow A=𝜙$, so (S1) is true.

(S2): $P(A)=1\Rightarrow n(A)=n(\Omega )\Rightarrow A=\Omega$, so (S2) is true.

Hence both (S1) and (S2) are true, which is NTA's answer (option A).

Remark: this rests on the classical definition used in JEE. For a continuous sample space it fails: choosing a point on a wire $[0,1]$, the event $A=\left \{\frac{1}{2}\right \}$ has $P(A)=0$ although $A\neq 𝜙$, and its complement has probability 1 although it is not $\Omega$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: The equation $x^{2}-4x+[x]+3=x[x]$, where $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer function, has :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{2}-4x+[x]+3=x[x]$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}-4x+[x]+3-x[x]=0$

$\Rightarrow (x-1)(x-3)-[x](x-1)=0$

$\Rightarrow (x-1)(x-[x]-3)=0$

$\therefore$ $x=1$

or

$x-[x]-3=0$

$\Rightarrow \{x\}-3=0$ [As $\{x\}=x-[x]$]

$\Rightarrow \{x\}=3$

But we know, $0\leq \{x\}<1$

$\therefore$ $\{x\}\neq 3$

$\therefore$ $x$ has only one solution in ($-\infty ,\infty$) which is $x=1$.

text: If A and B are two non-zero n $\times$ n matrices such that $\mathrm{A}^{2}+\mathrm{B}=\mathrm{A}^{2}\mathrm{B}$, then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given : $A^{2}+B=A^{2}B...(i)$

$\Rightarrow A^{2}+B-I=A^{2}B-I$

$\Rightarrow A^{2}B-A^{2}-B+I=I$

$\Rightarrow A^{2}(B-I)-I(B-I)=I$

$\Rightarrow \left (A^{2}-I\right )(B-I)=I$

$\therefore A^{2}-I$ is the inverse matrix of $B-I$ and vice versa.

So, $(B-I)\left (A^{2}-I\right )=I$

$\Rightarrow BA^{2}-B-A^{2}+I=I$

$\therefore A^{2}+B=BA^{2}...(ii)$

So, by (i) and (ii)

$A^{2}B=BA^{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: For three positive integers p, q, r, $x^{pq^{2}}=y^{qr}=z^{p^{2}r}$ and r = pq + 1 such that 3, 3 log${}_{y}x$, 3 log${}_{z}y$, 7 log${}_{x}z$ are in A.P. with common difference $\frac{1}{2}$. Then r-p-q is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The terms $3,3\log _{y}x,3\log _{z}y,7\log _{x}z$ are in A.P. with common difference $\dfrac{1}{2}$, so

$3\log _{y}x=\dfrac{7}{2},3\log _{z}y=4,7\log _{x}z=\dfrac{9}{2}.$

Thus $\log _{y}x=\dfrac{7}{6}$ and $\log _{z}y=\dfrac{4}{3}$, i.e. $x=y^{7/6}$ and $z=y^{3/4}$; these agree with $\log _{x}z=\dfrac{9}{14}$, since $\dfrac{7}{6}\times \dfrac{4}{3}\times \dfrac{9}{14}=1$.

Substituting in $x^{pq^{2}}=y^{qr}=z^{p^{2}r}$:

$y^{\frac{7}{6}pq^{2}}=y^{qr}=y^{\frac{3}{4}p^{2}r}\Rightarrow \dfrac{7}{6}pq^{2}=qr=\dfrac{3}{4}p^{2}r.$

First equality: $7pq=6r$. With $r=pq+1$, $7pq=6pq+6\Rightarrow pq=6$ and $r=7$.

Second equality: $q=\dfrac{3}{4}p^{2}$, so $p\times \dfrac{3}{4}p^{2}=6\Rightarrow p^{3}=8\Rightarrow p=2,q=3$.

$r-p-q=7-2-3=2$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
Let $f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} x^{2}\sin \left (\frac{1}{x}\right ) & ,\; x\neq 0 \\ 0 & ,\; x=0 \end{array} \right.$

Then at $x=0$
options: $f$ is continuous but $f^{'}$ is not continuous
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} x^{2}\sin \left (\frac{1}{x}\right ), & x\neq 0 \\ 0, & x=0 \end{array} \right.$

$\therefore$ $f^{'}(x)=2x\sin \left (\frac{1}{x}\right )-\cos \left (\frac{1}{x}\right )$

Now,

$\lim _{x\to 0}f^{'}(x)=\lim _{x\to 0}\left [2x\sin \left (\frac{1}{x}\right )-\cos \left (\frac{1}{x}\right )\right ]$

$=0-\lim _{x\to 0}\cos \left (\frac{1}{x}\right )$

= Does not exist

$\therefore$ $f^{'}(x)$ is discontinuous function at $x=0$.

L.H.D. $=\lim _{h\to 0^{+}}\frac{f(0-h)-f(0)}{-h}$

$=\lim _{h\to 0^{+}}\frac{f(-h)}{-h}$

$=\lim _{h\to 0^{+}}\frac{-h^{2}\sin \left (\frac{1}{h}\right )}{-h}=0$

R.H.D. $=\lim _{h\to 0^{+}}\frac{f(0+h)-f(0)}{h}$

$=\lim _{h\to 0^{+}}\frac{f(h)}{h}$

$=\lim _{h\to 0^{+}}\frac{h^{2}\sin \left (\frac{1}{h}\right )}{h}=0$

$\therefore$ L.H.D. = R.H.D.

$\Rightarrow f(x)$ is differentiable at $x=0$. So, f(x) is continuous.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: Let C be the largest circle centred at (2, 0) and inscribed in the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{36}+\frac{y^{2}}{16}=1$. If (1, $α$) lies on C, then 10 $α^{2}$ is equal to $____________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a point $(x,y)$ on $\dfrac{x^{2}}{36}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{16}=1$, $y^{2}=16-\dfrac{4x^{2}}{9}$, so its squared distance from $(2,0)$ is

$d^{2}=(x-2)^{2}+16-\frac{4x^{2}}{9}=\frac{5}{9}x^{2}-4x+20=\frac{5}{9}\left (x-\frac{18}{5}\right )^{2}+\frac{64}{5},-6\leq x\leq 6$

The largest circle centred at $(2,0)$ inside the ellipse touches it at the nearest point, so $r^{2}=\min d^{2}=\dfrac{64}{5}$, attained at $x=\dfrac{18}{5}\in [-6,6]$.

$(1,α)$ lies on C: $(1-2)^{2}+α^{2}=\dfrac{64}{5}\Rightarrow α^{2}=\dfrac{59}{5}$.

$10α^{2}=10\times \frac{59}{5}=118$

Hence, the answer is 118.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

solution.body:
Let, $I=\frac{8}{π}\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{(\cos x)^{2023}}{(\sin x)^{2023}+(\cos x)^{2023}}dx$ ..... (1)

Using formula,

$\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(x)dx=\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(a+b-x)dx$

$I=\frac{8}{π}\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{\left [\cos \left (\frac{π}{2}-x\right )\right ]^{2023}}{\left [\sin \left (\frac{π}{2}-x\right )\right ]^{2023}+\left [\cos \left (\frac{π}{2}-x\right )\right ]^{2023}}dx$

$=\frac{8}{π}\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{(\sin x)^{2023}}{(\cos x)^{2023}+(\sin x)^{2023}}dx$ ..... (2)

Adding equation (1) and (2), we get

$2I=\frac{8}{π}\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{(\sin x)^{2023}+(\cos x)^{2023}}{(\sin x)^{2023}+(\cos x)^{203}}dx$

$\Rightarrow 2I=\frac{8}{π}\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}dx$

$\Rightarrow 2I=\frac{8}{π}[x]_{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}$

$\Rightarrow 2I=\frac{8}{π}\times \frac{π}{2}$

$\Rightarrow 2I=4$

$\Rightarrow I=2$

text: The number of 9 digit numbers, that can be formed using all the digits of the number 123412341 so that the even digits occupy only even places, is $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Here, even digits are 2 and 4.

Number of digit "2" presents = 2

Number of digit "4" presents = 2

$\therefore$ Total even digits = 4


[IMG]


$\therefore$ Total 4 even places presents.

Number of ways to put those 4 digits in those 4 places $=\frac{{}^{4}C_{4}\times 4!}{2!2!}=\frac{4!}{2!2!}$

Now, remaining 5 digits (three 1 and two 3) can be put in those 5 places in $=\frac{{}^{5}C_{5}\times 5!}{3!2!}=\frac{5!}{3!2!}$ ways.

$\therefore$ Total possible 9 digit numbers

$=\frac{4!}{2!2!}\times \frac{5!}{3!2!}=60$
